title: Signature-led automated pin proposals for hardware-specific perf profiles (A100/H100/L40S/MI300)
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background:
We currently publish hand-curated performance profiles per model and per GPU SKU. This ticket proposes an automated, signature-led process that emits 'pin recommendations' for model variants per hardware (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) along with a scored confidence metric and suggested canary rollout parameters. The goal is to reduce manual effort, surface regressions earlier, and create an auditable artifact for release notes.

Scope / Goals:
- Define a deterministic latency/throughput signature extraction algorithm that covers cold/warm, seq lengths (64/256/1024), and batch shapes typical of our workloads.
- Compute a stability_score per (model, variant, sku) and produce a single pin proposal file (CSV + metadata) consumable by the pinning service.
- Emit regression flags (p99 delta, token throughput loss, memory pressure) with thresholds per SKU.
- Integrate with CI: run signature generation on every model onboarding PR and surface proposals in the PR checks.
- Provide a canary rollout recipe (small % traffic, 10k requests min, health checks) and automated rollback conditions.

Signature algorithm (proposal):
1) Collect sample suite across seq=[64,256,1024], batch=[1,4,8], cold vs warm (first token vs steady state). 1000 samples per shape where possible.
2) For each shape compute: p50, p90, p95, p99 latency; mean tokens/sec; memory_high_watermark.
3) Create a normalized vector per SKU by zscoring each metric against the SKU baseline for the model family.
4) Stability_score = 0.5 * (1 - normalized_p99_variation) + 0.3 * (normalized_throughput_score) + 0.2 * (1 - mem_variation_score). Scale to [0,100].
5) If stability_score >= 85 => pin_recommendation = STRONG. 70-85 => pin_recommendation = CAUTIOUS. <70 => pin_recommendation = AVOID_PIN.

Regression detection and thresholds (initial):
- p99 increase > 15% over pinned baseline => regressed=true
- throughput drop > 10% => regressed=true
- mem_high_watermark increase > 12% => regressed=true
These thresholds will be SKU-adjusted in a config file.

Canary rollout recipe (generated with proposal):
- Start: route 1% traffic for 24h, require >= 99.5% success, p99 within 10% of baseline.
- Ramp to 10% over 48h if checks pass.
- Full rollout only after 72h with no persistent regression flags.
- Automated rollback if any of the three regression checks trigger during canary window.

Acceptance criteria:
- A PR that runs signature extraction and posts a pin proposal artifact into the onboarding PR. See example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 for the CI hook design.
- A generated CSV per model (columns: model, variant, sku, stability_score, pin_recommendation, p99_delta_pct, throughput_delta_pct, mem_delta_pct, artifact_link).
- Dashboard tile that shows top 10 low-stability variants across SKUs. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/perf-signatures?ticket=ENG-97412.
- End-to-end test that simulates a controlled regression and triggers the rollback workflow.

Telemetry & Observability:
- Emit 'signature.generated' events to analytics with tags (model, variant, sku, sample_count, stability_score).
- Add perf-signature diff view to Console with quick links to run extra samples.
- Track pin adoption rate and number of manual overrides as a health metric for the automation.

Trade-offs / Notes:
- Benefit: faster onboarding and more consistent, auditable pin decisions.
- Risk: over-reliance on synthetic signature suite may miss real-world workload shapes. Mitigation: require a 'real-traffic verification' gate for Strong pins in production.
- Performance variability across cloud instances for the same SKU (noisy neighbors) can bias scores — solution: aggregate over at least 10 distinct hosts where possible.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Data model and CSV schema (this ticket) + config for SKU thresholds.
2) CI job to run sample-suite and commit signature artifact to PR (reuse existing perf harness).
3) Scoring service that computes stability_score and emits proposal.
4) Console integration for review/override and canary wizard generation.
5) Rollout and monitoring (2-week dogfood with internal models).

Progress log / updates:
- 2025-02-10 (Aisha): Drafted algorithm and acceptance criteria, added threshold suggestions. Created initial CSV schema.
- 2025-02-17 (Luis): Implemented signature extractor prototype in perf-harness branch (PR #4821). Ran sample-suite for 3 internal models on A100/H100 — raw artifacts uploaded to gs://redwood-perf/ENG-97412/.
- 2025-02-21 (Infra): Observability events stubbed; 'signature.generated' event added to telemetry schema.
- 2025-02-25 (Aisha): Validated scoring on historical onboarding runs; stability_score correlated with manual pin decisions for 86% of cases.
- 2025-02-28 (PM review): Product asks to add explicit canary time windows per SKU. Updated canary recipe accordingly.
- 2025-03-01 (Luis): Opened this ticket for engineering review; attaching PR and dashboard links.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Finalize SKU-specific threshold tuning methodology and who owns that config (SRE or Model Onboarding team).
- Determine retention policy for generated signatures (current proposal: 90 days, unless tied to a pinned release).
- Decide whether 'STRONG' pins auto-apply for internal tenants or always require a human approval step.

Rollout plan and timeline:
- Week 1 (now): Merge CI hook + signature extractor prototype to staging.
- Week 2: Enable scoring service and emit proposals to onboarding PRs for internal models. Dogfood for 2 weeks.
- Week 4: Console review flow + canary wizard available to internal platform teams.
- Week 6: Gradual enablement for public onboarding with opt-out flag.

Related artifacts and reading:
- HW signature spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/HW+Signature+Spec
- Perf harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
- Sample artifacts: gs://redwood-perf/ENG-97412/sample-signatures.csv

Next steps (immediate):
- Review algorithm and thresholds (SRE + Applied ML).
- Get sign-off on canary windows per SKU.
- Add tests for noisy-host aggregation and ensure score stability across runs.

Owner: Luis Ortega
Reviewers: Aisha Raman, Priya Kulkarni (SRE), Mark Chen (Applied ML)

This ticket is intentionally conservative on auto-apply behavior; initial rollout focuses on surfacing high-confidence recommendations and reducing manual triage time.
